notes.body:
I think  
```
ERROR: The remote file either doesn't exist, is unauthorized, or is forbidden for url 
'https://sourceforge.net/projects/docbook/files/docbook-xsl/1.79.1/docbook-xsl-1.79.1.zip/download'. Exception  
calling "GetResponse" with "0" argument(s): "The request was aborted: Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel." 
```
is caused when sourceforge is busy.  
  
!8633 - `winflexbison3` had the same issue and changing to latest version which is hosted on Github cleared up issue.  
I haven't cherry picked to 3.6 yet. Here is a winflexbison3 download error on 3.6: https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/actions/runs/3373877720/jobs/5598892155  
  
https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/docbook-bundle  
I put in a comment to the `docbook-bundle` creator on `community.chocolatey.org` about changing to a different download location.

Well... the message

> The request was aborted: Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel.

is pretty confusing, then.
Agreed. "Could not create channel." would be less confusing.

@chuckcraft do you think my change just accidentally fixed the problem? If it's a matter of sourceforge load, wouldn't it be random? Instead it's not completing anymore, 100%. With my change it worked fine 2 out of 2 tries. What do you think? Do we want to give it another spin?

@crondaemon If you look at the Windows run history it appears random:  
https://github.com/wireshark/wireshark/actions/workflows/windows.yml?query=  
  
The Github actions seem to be almost a "nice to have" but not core production so wouldn't hurt to experiment to see if setting `Tls12` makes a difference.  
  
Github has [Caching dependencies to speed up workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/caching-dependencies-to-speed-up-workflows) but does not include `choco`.  
I'm not sure if the licenses for the items in [docbook-bundle](https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/docbook-bundle) would allow making a copy of them in a new Github project them referencing either from the build files or updating the `choco` to download from the Github copies.

> The Github actions seem to be almost a "nice to have" but not core production so wouldn't hurt to experiment to see if setting `Tls12` makes a difference.

Agreed. But I would also merge the winflexbison installation with other packages. I don't know if it will perform better, but it's cleaner. Before it was separated because of the version.

Pushing an update.

> I put in a comment to the `docbook-bundle` creator on `community.chocolatey.org` about changing to a different download location.

I tried creating a docbook-bundle package that uses [release 1.79.2, which is hosted on GitHub](https://github.com/docbook/xslt10-stylesheets/releases/tag/release%2F1.79.2), but the catalogs included in the 1.79.1 release reference docbook.sourceforge.net URLs, while the catalogs included with the 1.79.2 release reference cdn.docbook.org URLs. Trying to switch between them results in "failed to load external entity" in my build VM.

I think they swapped the namespaced vs non-namespaced packages, which seems like a big jump for a micro release.

I *think* I got the package switched to 1.79.2 / GitHub. It works from a fresh install and when upgrading from the existing package in my Windows VM. It should show up on chocolatey.org once it passes the approval process.

https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/docbook-bundle#versionhistory  
  
It currently as state `Ready` and is waiting to be `Approved`.  

https://docs.chocolatey.org/en-us/community-repository/moderation/#reviewer-moderator-process

"The LicenseUrl element in the nuspec file ..."  

Are the nuspec files visible somewhere?

It's been approved.

> Are the nuspec files visible somewhere?

Each Chocolatey package has a "package source" link. The Docbook bundle link is https://github.com/geraldcombs/chocolatey-packages.
Another solution to this would be to ditch the XSLT pipeline and use https://github.com/owenh000/asciidoctor-multipage to generate our chunked / multipage guides.
Are the commits in this MR still valuable? The package join, is, IMO, the TLS one, I don't know. It should not hurt, but I'm not sure whether it makes sense to join or not.

I would like to see some number of clean builds with the new docbook before closing this issue.  
Unfortunately there is another issue currently with libsmi that broke the build.  
  
https://community.chocolatey.org/packages/cmake#versionhistory  
cmake changed from `v3.24.3` to `v3.25.0`

Need a way to force old behavior of looking at `.lib`???  

```
< -- Generating build using CMake 3.24.3^M
---
> -- Generating build using CMake 3.25.0^M
1417c1405
< -- Found SMI: C:/wireshark-libs/wireshark-win64-libs/libsmi-svn-40773-win64ws/lib/libsmi-2.lib  ^M
---
> -- Found SMI: C:/wireshark-libs/wireshark-win64-libs/libsmi-svn-40773-win64ws/lib/libsmi.a  ^M
1432c1420
< -- Found ZLIB: C:/wireshark-libs/wireshark-win64-libs/vcpkg-export-20220726-1-win64ws/installed/x64-windows/lib/zlib.lib  ^M
---
> -- Found ZLIB: C:/hostedtoolcache/windows/strawberry-perl/5.30.3/x64/c/lib/libz.a  ^M
3962c3950,3972
```
  
https://cmake.org/cmake/help/latest/release/3.25.html  
> On Windows, when targeting the MSVC ABI, the find_library() command now accepts .a file names after first considering .lib. This is symmetric with existing behavior when targeting the GNU ABI, in which the command accepts .lib file names after first considering .a.

For the SMI issue it looks like we can either remove `libsmi.a` from the archive or only set SMI_NAMES to `libsmi-2` for MSVC targets.

Adding any and all Strawberry library directories CMAKE_IGNORE_PATH or CMAKE_IGNORE_PREFIX_PATH should fix the zlib issue and might let us simplify some of our CMake modules.

I'm rebuilding my Windows dev system so will be a good time to experiment.  
If we're not loading a specific version of `cmake` from chocolatey could it be possible to use the `cmake` that can be added with the `Visual Studio` install?

> the TLS one, I don't know.

I'd vote against it. It shouldn't be necessary any more, and we never know when someone will find a serious flaw in TLS 1.2.

https://github.com/bubbasnmp/wireshark/actions/runs/3595487350  
After the changes made to cmakelists it works ok with latest - cmake v3.25.1
If choco installs a lower version, we need to require a specific version, hence we need 2 different lines.

The specific version was added (!8893) when the latest Chocolatey version moved to 3.25 and broke the build. Gerald fixed those issues in !8941 (and cherry picked to 3.6 and 4.0). I think running with latest version (no version specified to `cinst`) will catch issues that might come up for others creating a build system from the notes in the WSDG.  
  
Same as there was a specific version of winflexbison3 used for a while but it now works with the latest - !8633.
